prompt: At 120 Hz, how many milliseconds does each frame have? Answer to one decimal place.
What does Android measure before it shows an "App isn't responding" dialog?

choices.text: A frame that took longer than 16.7 ms
choices.why: A slow frame is dropped; nothing is reported to the person.

choices.text: A disk read on the main thread
choices.why: StrictMode reports that in a debug build; it is not an ANR.

choices.text: An input event not handled within 5 seconds
choices.why: Right. That is an ANR.

choices.text: The battery level during a query
choices.why: Battery has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Match each platform's signal to what it reacts to.

pairs.right: a disk read on the main thread, in a debug build
the iOS watchdog ending a slow launch
a query on the main thread

prompt: A query takes 4 ms on the developer's phone. Why does the lesson still say the question is which thread waits for it?

choices.text: Old phones, more rows: 40 ms
choices.why: Right. On a five-year-old phone with three years of sessions it takes ten times as long; the developer's phone is the best case.

choices.text: Queries take longer the second time
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: 4 ms is already over the frame budget
choices.why: It is under 16.7 ms; the problem is elsewhere.

choices.text: The main thread is slower than the others
choices.why: It is not slower; it is the one that draws.

prompt: Why does blocking.ts report that no frame was drawn while the query ran?

choices.text: Node only fires timers every 100 ms
choices.why: The 100 ms is the delay before the query starts.

choices.text: The timer was cleared before the query
choices.why: It is cleared after.

choices.text: The query was too fast to span a frame
choices.why: It counts to three million so that it is slow anywhere.

choices.text: A synchronous call holds the thread
choices.why: Right. better-sqlite3 holds the only JavaScript thread until it returns.

prompt: Why does blocking.ts print "none" or "at least one" rather than the number of frames, or the time the query took?

choices.text: Node cannot measure time
choices.why: It can; the choice is about what repeats.

choices.text: Neither repeats across computers
choices.why: Right. The transcript has to be the same on yours, and whether a frame was drawn does not depend on the machine.

choices.text: The number is always zero
choices.why: In the worker version it is not.

choices.text: Frames are counted only on phones
choices.why: The timer counts them here.

prompt: A team makes the slow query faster with an index, and leaves it on the main thread. What remains true, according to the lesson?

choices.text: Nothing; an indexed query cannot drop a frame
choices.why: On a slow phone with a large file it still can.

choices.text: It is still a disk read on the thread that draws
choices.why: Right. Efficiency and where the work runs are separate questions.

choices.text: Room would now allow it without allowMainThreadQueries
choices.why: Room refuses main-thread queries whatever their plan.

choices.text: The spinner will now turn
choices.why: It is drawn by the same thread, which is busy for as long as the query runs.

prompt: Why does query-worker.ts open its own database connection instead of receiving the main thread's?

choices.text: Workers cannot import packages
choices.why: It imports better-sqlite3 in its first line.

choices.text: Two connections make the query twice as fast
choices.why: The query takes as long either way.

choices.text: The main thread's connection is read-only
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson makes it read-only.

choices.text: A connection belongs to the thread that opened it
choices.why: Right. Threads share data only by messages here.

prompt: In off-main.ts, what changed compared with blocking.ts?

choices.text: The thread that runs the query
choices.why: Right. Everything else is identical.

choices.text: The frames are 32 ms apart
choices.why: 16 ms in both.

choices.text: The query counts to fewer rows
choices.why: Three million in both.

choices.text: The database is on disk instead of in memory
choices.why: Both are in memory.

prompt: Which of these keep a query off the main thread? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a suspend DAO function in Room
choices.why: Room runs it on its own executors.

choices.text: a method of a @ModelActor in SwiftData
choices.why: The actor owns a context of its own.

choices.text: getAllAsync in expo-sqlite
choices.why: It runs on a native thread.

choices.text: getAllSync in expo-sqlite
choices.why: That is blocking.ts again.

prompt: While the worker writes a sync, the main thread reads the week. What does the lesson say keeps the read from seeing half a sync?

choices.text: The worker's messages arrive in order
choices.why: Order of messages says nothing about what the database holds mid-write.

choices.text: Running both on the main thread after all
choices.why: That brings the frozen screen back.

choices.text: Transactions, and WAL
choices.why: Right. Transactions on both sides, with WAL letting one read while the other writes: the reader sees the last committed state.

choices.text: Copying the database to the worker first
choices.why: A copy is a second database, out of date as soon as it is made.

prompt: How many index entries did the OFFSET query walk to return page 301, in the lesson's run?
Why does the keyset query order by `(date, id)` rather than by `date` alone?

choices.text: Many sessions share a date, so date alone cannot say where a page ended
choices.why: Right. No two rows share both.

choices.text: SQLite cannot sort by one column
choices.why: It can; the order would just not be unique.

choices.text: The id makes the index smaller
choices.why: It makes it larger, slightly.

choices.text: Row values need two columns
choices.why: The reason is uniqueness, not the syntax.

prompt: A list that asks for the fifty rows after the last one shown is using ___ paging.
A sync deletes one session dated before the page the person is reading, between page 301 and page 302. By OFFSET, what does page 302 do?

choices.text: Repeats the last row of page 301
choices.why: That is what an inserted row does.

choices.text: Shows the same rows as by keyset
choices.why: Every row after the deletion has moved one place back.

choices.text: Skips one row that is never shown
choices.why: Right. The rows moved back one position, and the offset did not.

choices.text: Fails, because an offset must point at an existing row
choices.why: An offset is a count; it fails at nothing.

prompt: Put in order what happens in off-main.ts.
items: the screen timer starts counting frames
the main thread posts the query to the worker
the worker runs it while frames keep being drawn
the answer arrives as a message, and the timer stops

prompt: A React Native planner moves its query to getAllAsync, and the history screen still takes two seconds to show. What does the lesson say is left to do?

choices.text: Go back to getAllSync, which is faster
choices.why: It is the same query, and it would freeze the screen too.

choices.text: Read one page at a time
choices.why: Right. Off the main thread and less of it: the lesson does both.

choices.text: Nothing; the screen no longer stutters
choices.why: It no longer stutters, and the person still waits.

choices.text: Add a second worker thread
choices.why: Two threads do not make one large query smaller.

prompt: In React Native, what keeps running while the JavaScript thread is busy?

choices.text: Touch handling
choices.why: Touches queue up behind the busy thread.

choices.text: Animations driven from JavaScript
choices.why: Those freeze.

choices.text: Every timer set with setInterval
choices.why: Those run on the JavaScript thread and wait with it.

choices.text: Native animations
choices.why: Right. They run outside the JavaScript thread.
